processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting and casting into cylindrical copper moulds
processing_steps.cooling_medium: cylindrical copper moulds (32 mm diameter × 186 mm length)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: As-cast terminal state; no further heat treatment reported.

processing_steps.method: spark erosion cutting and surface grinding
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Mechanical test specimens cut from cast ingots by spark erosion along the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction); specimen surfaces ground.

structures.overall_structure: As-cast two-phase microstructure: Fe-Al (A2 bcc) matrix dendrites with TiC precipitates

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression: (6×6×10) mm³; tension: flat (3.5×5) mm² cross-section, 15 mm gauge length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: specimens cut along longitudinal (casting) direction; surfaces ground; Brinell hardness with load 62.5 g and 2.5 mm diameter ball

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Room-temperature compression: parabolic work hardening behaviour (Fig. 2a, curve 2). Room-temperature tension: linear elastic loading followed by abrupt fracture between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines (Fig. 3a, curve 2).

strain_hardening_rate.value: parabolic work hardening behaviour (typical for most disordered polycrystalline metallic materials)

measurement_conditions.temperature: elevated temperatures up to 800 °C (tension additionally at 650 °C and 800 °C)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression: (6×6×10) mm³; tension: flat (3.5×5) mm² cross-section, 15 mm gauge length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: held 30 min at testing temperature before loading; temperature checked by NiCr–Ni thermocouple on specimen surface

yield_strength.value: yield stress decreases monotonically with increasing temperature (no yield stress anomaly); near the 500 MPa gridline at room temperature and converging to 0–100 MPa by 800 °C (Fig. 5, no numeric labels)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Matrix Brinell hardness and yield stress in compression at room temperature

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of fracture surfaces
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-Hitachi S-530, 20 kV, working distance 15 mm, secondary electrons (SE)
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigation of fracture surfaces of ruptured tensile specimens
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C shows coarse transgranular cleavage facets and a large smooth cleavage plane (Fig. 4b).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: load 62.5 g, indentation ball 2.5 mm diameter
ZWICK 1474 universal testing machine; deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 800 °C) in protective argon atmosphere at elevated temperatures
characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of yield stress, work hardening and ductility
characterization_methods.key_findings: Room temperature: yield stress in compression 485 MPa, yield stress in tension 420 MPa, total elongation 3.3%.

unmapped_findings: Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C exhibits the highest room-temperature ductility (≈3.3%) of all Fe-15Al-based alloys [b0035].
Room-temperature fracture mode is TGC (transgranular cleavage); SEM fractograph (Fig. 4b) shows coarse transgranular cleavage facets and a large smooth cleavage plane [b0033, b0035, figure_004].

At 650 °C and 800 °C, compressive yield stress exceeds tensile yield stress (tension–compression asymmetry) for Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C; no numeric labels are printed for this alloy in Figs. 7 and 8 [b0040, figure_007, figure_008].
Room-temperature tension–compression asymmetry: yield stress in compression (485 MPa) is higher than yield stress in tension (420 MPa) [b0029, b0033].
A good correlation between matrix hardness and yield stress in compression was observed for Fe-15Al-based alloys with Ti and V [b0023].
